analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free is caused by stale ownership/state in the chaining loop after splitting a regexp AST. `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point` frees the split gap node (`child`) and may leave `remainder_re_ast` from a previous iteration unchanged when no new split occurs. In `yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration`, the loop then destroys `re_ast` and assigns `re_ast = remainder_re_ast` without clearing/resetting `remainder_re_ast` each iteration, so a previously destroyed AST pointer can be reused and later destroyed again, leading to UAF in `yr_re_node_destroy` during AST teardown.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered when parsing a regexp string in the rules fuzzer path (`yr_lex_parse_rules_string` -> parser reduce string declaration) that enters chaining/splitting logic (`yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point`) at least once, then iterates again with stale `remainder_re_ast` state. The PoC regex `/.{,}?/` in a string declaration drives this path: parse regexp AST, attempt split at chaining point, write string, destroy current AST, then loop with stale remainder pointer and eventually destroy already-freed nodes.
